results.content: # Service interruption and customer withdrawal in the congested facility location problem. The congested facility location problem with unreliable servers is modeled. This research addresses the location problem of congested facilities, assuming service interruptions and customer withdrawals. As a result, strategic planning should take server reliability and facility congestion seriously, and in the event of service interruption or congestion, customer behavior should be considered. Location decisions can significantly impact how demand is allocated to facilities, the congestion within facilities, and the percentage of customers who experience service interruptions. If facilities are not properly located, consumer demand will not be uniformly spread among them, resulting in congestion and long lines at facilities with high demand volumes. This paper examines the problem of locating congested facilities with repairable servers based on the premise that server interruption results in customer loss. For the first time, Drezner (1987) raised the issue of reliability in facility location problems. Besides, the first model for the unreliable facility location problem was proposed by Snyder & Daskin (2005). In their research, the P-median problem and the uncapacitated fixed-charge location problem (UFLP) were formulated with the assumption of the possibility of facility. The facility location problem is investigated in this section under three underlying assumptions: congestion, service interruption, and customer withdrawal. The facility location problem with the risk of interruption can be reduced to the well-known classical location-allocation problem. results.content: # Model and solution for capacitated facility location problem PDF "You do not have access to this PDF") Hongtao Yu; Liqun Gao; Yanhua Lei # Alerts ## Abstract: This paper presents a new model for capacitated facility location problem, where serve radius and economic benefit are considered. In the new model, the objective is to m...Show More ## Metadata ## Abstract: This paper presents a new model for capacitated facility location problem, where serve radius and economic benefit are considered. So the capacitated facility location problem can be translated into multiple knapsack problem. **Published in:** 2012 24th Chinese Control and Decision Conference (CCDC) **Date of Conference:** 23-25 May 2012 **Date Added to IEEE *Xplore*:** 19 July 2012 ## ISSN Information: **DOI:** 10.1109/CCDC.2012.6244284 ### 1 INTRODUCTION The capacitated facility location problem is an important class of combinatorial optimizations in which the objective is to minimize the total cost, including the opening cost of plants and allocation cost of assigning products to customer without violating the capacity restrictions of the plants. So the capacitated facility location problem is one of critical problems for commercial facilities, e.g. shops and stores. In 1963, Cooper [1] studies the basic facility location problem which is to decide locations of warehouses and allocation of customers demand given the locations and demand of customers. Since then, many extensions of facility location problem have been studied by many researches, capacitated facilitated locations is just one of them. [3] consider a new capacitated plant location problem with customer and supplier matching. [5] present a new hybrid algorithm for a classical capacitated plant location problem. Chen and Ting [7] describe a multiple ant colony system to solve the single source capacitated facility location problem. [8] use genetic algorithm to solve capacitated plant location problem. Amiri [9] develop a special two-echelon capacitated location problem which allows for multiple levels of capacities available to the warehouses and plants. A limitation of most existing studies on capacitated facility location problem is that customers can be served no matter how far apart they are, so we present a new capacitated facility location model. Because the capacitated facility location problem is a NP-hard problem [10], we use harmony search algorithm and greedy algorithm to solve it.
